svg.title: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + PKCE
svg.desc: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + PKCE. The standard sign-in flow for web, mobile and single-page apps: code via the browser, tokens via the back channel. Step 1, Authorization request: The App keeps a random code_verifier and sends only its SHA-256 hash, code_challenge, to /authorize. Step 2, Sign in & consent: The user signs in and consents. The code comes back through the browser, visible in the URL. Step 3, Code exchange: Back channel: the App sends code + code_verifier. The server checks the hash and issues tokens. Step 4, Call the API: The App calls the API with the access token. The API validates the JWT itself and returns the data.

g.text: The App keeps a random code_verifier and sends only its SHA-256 hash, code_challenge, to /authorize.
The user signs in and consents. The code comes back through the browser, visible in the URL.
Back channel: the App sends code + code_verifier. The server checks the hash and issues tokens.
The App calls the API with the access token. The API validates the JWT itself and returns the data.
front channel: code is in the URL
stolen code without the verifier → invalid_grant
